text:
maria: quick check — running into weird streaming disconnects when we rotate service-account JWTs every 15m. Node SDK opens a streaming socket to the inference endpoint, we refresh the token in the background and update Authorization header, but the socket drops after the first token swap. anyone seen this pattern or have recommended approach?

aj: seen this before. usually streaming endpoints expect the auth to be stable for the life of the connection. refreshing the header mid-connection often requires a re-auth handshake, not just swapping the header var. how are you applying the new token?

maria: we're doing a fetch for a new signed JWT and then calling ws.headers['authorization'] = `Bearer ${token}` before the next send. no explicit reconnect.

priya: that explains it — websockets won't redo the HTTP auth handshake after upgrade. options: 1) do a silent reconnect with jitter and resume token, or 2) use a session-level ephemeral credential that we rotate less frequently (e.g., mint a short-lived session token from the SA that is valid for the streaming session length).

aj: +1 on resume vs replace in-place. our recommendation for SDKs: background refresh should proactively open a new connection and stream-race to avoid in-flight disruption. algo: if token_ttl < threshold, open new ws with new token, wait until 'ready', then gracefully switch. add slightly randomized backoff to avoid thundering herd.

maria: that makes sense. any code example patterns for node/python?

aj: node pseudo:
```
async function ensureConn() {
  if (conn && tokenExp - now > 30_000) return conn
  const newToken = await refreshJwt()
  const newConn = await openStream({ headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${newToken}` } })
  await waitForReady(newConn)
  conn?.closeGracefully()
  conn = newConn
}
setInterval(ensureConn, 10_000)
```

priya: python sketch:
```
async def ensure_conn():
    global conn, token_exp
    if conn and token_exp - now() > 30:
        return
    token = await refresh_jwt()
    new_conn = await open_stream(auth_header=f"Bearer {token}")
    await wait_for_ready(new_conn)
    await conn.close() if conn else None
    conn = new_conn
asyncio.create_task(periodic(ensure_conn, 10))
```

tom: also double-check the SA scopes/audience. if you mint a JWT with an audience tied to a project or org (aud claim), swapping to a token minted for a different project will cause the server to drop session. keep the same audience for session tokens. if you need to change projects, do a full reconnect.

maria: good call — we actually had a mix where the refresh path accidentally used the default audience (org-level) and the initial token used project-scoped aud. that would explain the immediate drop.

aj: last note: add exponential backoff + jitter on reconnect attempts and limit retries on permanent auth failures (401/403). emit a metric when reconnects happen so we can correlate with token rotations.

infra-bot: deploy-notify: streaming-service (canary) rolled back 1h ago due to auth-handshake flakiness — related alerts: stream.disconnects > 200/min in us-west-2.

priya: thanks — sounds like two action items: 1) ensure refresh path uses same audience/claims as initial mint, 2) implement proactive connection swap (race & graceful close) plus retry/backoff. anyone want to pair later today?

maria: I can pair at 4pm PT. i'll also run an audit of where tokens are minted (node lambda vs python backend).

tom: i'll drop a snippet in the SDK repo demonstrating the race-reconnect pattern and a small test harness.

aj: I can add metrics hooks to the console dashboard for reconnects and token-claim mismatches. :thumbsup:

maria: great — thanks all. tagging this thread for follow-up after the 4pm sync. :sparkles:
